content.text: Squarespace Horizontal Scrolling | The complete no code tutorial

It can be hard to slow down your site visitors so they don’t scroll past your best content. Horizontal scrolling changes things up, guiding people through your site in an entirely new way that feels immersive and compelling. I’m Loren from SquareKicker, and I’m going to show you how easy it is to add Horizontal Scrolling to your next Squarespace site.
To create a Horizontal Scrolling track, you’ll need at least two Squarespace sections. (laptop)
REVERSE
Now by default, your sections will scroll from left to right as visitors move down the page. But if you want to reverse the direction, simply enable Reverse! (laptop)
FLUID
Next, let’s look at Fluid. (laptop)
And when Fluid is enabled, you’ll also get to customise this background color. (laptop)
STACK
Another option is Stack. (laptop)

This creates a really unique visual effect where previous sections remain partially visible while new sections continue moving into view. And this offers very cool options when used alongside section width, which I’ll show you toward the end of the video.
SPEED
You can also control the speed of the Horizontal Scrolling effect. The speed slider lets you slow down or speed up how quickly sections move across the screen. (laptop)
Lower speeds create a much more immersive storytelling experience, while faster speeds feel more dynamic and responsive.
FIXED BACK
Another really popular option is Fixed background. (laptop)
Mobile and Tablet Behavior

Now let’s look at device behavior. Horizontal Scrolling has flexible options for smaller screen sizes so your site looks great everywhere. (scroll to section) Horizontal Scrolling is automatically disabled on mobile by default because this type of interaction usually feels more natural on larger screens. But you have full control over this and can choose to:
Enable Horizontal Scrolling on smaller screens
Switch back to standard vertical scrolling - To do this you would select ‘Disabled’ on each screen size. (show example tablet)
Or you can choose to completely hide the whole track on certain devices. If you do this, you could create specific sections that are only visible on tablet and mobile, using the Visibility tool.
This gives you a lot of flexibility when designing responsive experiences across different screen sizes.
Advanced designs
(enable Stack in advance before starting)
One of the most exciting aspects of Horizontal Scrolling is combining it with other SquareKicker tools.
As I mentioned earlier, section width can be adjusted, which looks really great when Stack is enabled.
Instead of every section taking up the full screen width, you can create sections anywhere from 25% to 100% wide, or even set custom widths. (laptop)
This creates visual hierarchy, emphasises certain content, or creates repeating layout patterns throughout the scroll track.
Now the last thing I want  to show you is how Horizontal scrolling can interact with Scroll Effects. (laptop)
Whether you’re creating portfolio showcases, or product presentations, the Horizontal Scrolling tool makes this incredibly easy with just a few clicks and no custom code.
Thanks for watching, and we can’t wait to see what you create with SquareKicker.
